issues.title: GetMsg() infinite loop - missing timeout
symptoms: Backend sends message but door never responds
No new XIM messages after initial JH_INIT
Door process stays alive but unresponsive
issues.rootCause: Door calls GetMsg() in blocking mode without timeout or signal handling. If no message arrives, door hangs forever.
issues.solution: Add timeout using Wait() with signal mask to allow breaking out of GetMsg() loop

codeExample.before:
// WRONG - blocks forever
XIMMessage *msg = (XIMMessage *)GetMsg(replyPort);

issues.title: JH_SM sent before JH_INIT received
symptoms: Door appears to send output but nothing displays
XIM log shows JH_SM at position 0 or 1
issues.rootCause: Door sends messages before receiving JH_INIT from backend. XIM protocol requires JH_INIT first.
issues.solution: Add initialization state check. Wait for JH_INIT before sending any messages.

issues.title: Memory leak - AllocMem without FreeMem
symptoms: Door crashes after running for extended period
Multiple AllocMem calls in logs with no corresponding FreeMem
issues.rootCause: Door allocates memory but never frees it. Each door invocation leaks memory.
issues.solution: Implement cleanup routine that frees all allocated memory. Call on exit and error paths.

issues.title: Slow keystroke response (>2000ms)
symptoms: Multiple seconds between JH_HK and next JH_SM
issues.rootCause: Door performs blocking I/O or expensive computation in keystroke handler
issues.solution: Optimize keystroke handler. Move slow operations (file I/O, database queries) to background or async.

issues.title: Rapid-fire message loop (>100 msgs/sec)
issues.rootCause: Infinite loop sending messages without delay or exit condition
issues.solution: Add loop exit condition or delay between messages

issues.title: Door crashes immediately on startup
symptoms: Illegal instruction or segfault in logs
issues.rootCause: Startup crash due to: null pointer dereference, illegal instruction, missing library, or corrupt binary
issues.solution: Check door logs for crash details. Verify library dependencies. Test with vamos for reference.

issues.title: Buffer overrun - data length mismatch
symptoms: Declared dataLen doesn't match actual data
issues.rootCause: Door miscalculates buffer length. Common when mixing strlen() with fixed buffers or forgetting null terminator.
issues.solution: Always use actual data length. Double-check string length calculations.

issues.title: No JH_INIT message received
symptoms: Backend logs show "failed to send JH_INIT"
issues.rootCause: Backend failed to send JH_INIT. Usually due to: reply port not created, door not registered, or crash before message sent.
issues.solution: Check backend logs for door startup errors. Verify reply port creation. Ensure door registered with backend.

issues.title: Door not responding to messages
symptoms: Door sends few or no responses
Large gap between sent and received counts
issues.rootCause: Door message handler not processing all message types, or GetMsg() loop has logic error
issues.solution: Ensure message loop handles all message types. Add default case to log unknown types.

issues.title: No JH_TERMINATE - door exited abruptly
issues.rootCause: Door exited without waiting for JH_TERMINATE. User may have killed process or door crashed.
issues.solution: Wait for JH_TERMINATE in main loop. Handle Ctrl+C gracefully.

issues.title: Required library not found
issues.rootCause: Door tries to open library that doesn't exist or isn't in library path
issues.solution: Check library name spelling. Verify library exists in Libs/ directory. Check LibraryManager logs.

issues.title: Null pointer dereference
issues.rootCause: Code dereferences NULL pointer without checking
issues.solution: Always check pointers before dereferencing. Add NULL checks after allocations and function calls.

issues.title: Stack overflow - too much recursion or local vars
issues.rootCause: Function uses too much stack space or recursion depth is excessive
issues.solution: Use heap allocation for large buffers. Limit recursion depth. Reduce local variable size.

issues.title: Required file not found
symptoms: Door tries to open file but fails
issues.rootCause: Door expects file that doesn't exist. Path may be wrong or file not copied to BBS.
issues.solution: Check file path case-sensitivity. Verify file exists. Use AmigaFS for path resolution.

issues.title: Endianness issue - reading multi-byte values
issues.rootCause: Amiga 68K is big-endian. Reading little-endian data produces wrong values.
issues.solution: Use big-endian reads for all multi-byte values. XIM protocol is big-endian.

codeExample.before:
// WRONG - assumes little-endian
ULONG value = *(ULONG*)buffer;  // May be wrong endian

issues.title: String not null-terminated
issues.rootCause: Buffer copied without null terminator. strlen() reads past end of buffer.
issues.solution: Always null-terminate strings. Use strncpy() with explicit null.

issues.title: Using wrong node number
symptoms: Multiple doors interfere with each other
User sees output from different node
issues.rootCause: Door hardcoded node number or didn't read it from JH_INIT
issues.solution: Read node number from JH_INIT message. Store globally and use for all messages.

codeExample.before:
// WRONG - hardcoded
ULONG nodeNum = 1;  // What if running on node 2?

issues.title: Resource leak - file/library not closed
issues.rootCause: Door opens files/libraries but doesn't close them on all code paths
issues.solution: Close all resources on exit and error paths. Use cleanup function.

issues.title: Race condition - shared data access
issues.rootCause: Multiple code paths access shared data without synchronization
issues.solution: Use semaphores or forbid/permit to protect critical sections

codeExample.before:
// WRONG - no synchronization
globalCounter++;  // Race if called from multiple places

issues.title: ANSI escape sequence malformed
issues.rootCause: ANSI escape sequence has wrong format or missing terminator
issues.solution: Follow ANSI standard. Test sequences. Use AnsiUtil helper.

codeExample.before:
// WRONG - missing 'm'
sendMessage("\x1b[31Text");  // Should be \x1b[31m
codeExample.after:
// CORRECT - complete sequence
sendMessage("\x1b[31mRed Text\x1b[0m");  // Proper ANSI
